Sub-Domains within Physical Infrastructure

_To be drafted from D13 verified — a one-paragraph framing of what the seven sub-domains are and how they decompose the domain. The decomposition is hybrid (population-cum-instrument): six substantive sub-domains organized by infrastructure system, plus a seventh that synthesizes the cross-cutting federal funding architecture._

1 Transit & Mobility _To be drafted from D13 SD1 — SEPTA-centric: the September 2025 fare action and June 2025 service action; ADA Title II accessibility (the 46% station-accessibility gap); paratransit eligibility; transit access as labor market access._ 2 Water & Stormwater _To be drafted from D13 SD2 — PWD as enterprise utility; the lead service line replacement pilot; SDWA / LCRR / LCRI compliance; basement flooding service requests; CSO architecture; pre-1986 housing stock as the structurally relevant cohort for lead exposure._ 3 Roads, Bridges & Pedestrian Infrastructure _To be drafted from D13 SD3 — High Injury Network concentration; PDPH UC metric documentation of the 2.4x KSI rate disparity; sidewalk vintage and curb ramp ADA Title II compliance variation; mobility-impaired pedestrian pathway analysis._ 4 Solid Waste & Sanitation _To be drafted from D13 SD4 — Streets Department FY25 budget expansion; PPD Environmental Crimes Unit and SWEEP officer NOV process; vacant lot concentration as structural opportunity geography for illegal dumping; criminal-vs-civil enforcement architecture._ 5 School Buildings _To be drafted from D13 SD5 — SDP capital architecture and the 85 buildings rated poor or unsatisfactory; AHERA enforcement against SDP without compensating compliance financing (the federal-floor / compliance-financing structural mismatch surfaced as carry-forward A2); the 70,000 empty seats and the 17 proposed closures._ 6 Parks & Open Space _To be drafted from D13 SD6 — PPR-managed park and recreation infrastructure; the 14%/36% park space equity gap; the 5%-to-45% tree canopy range and the 22-degree heat differential; TPL ParkScore Equity score of 72/100; cooling center activation during heat events._ 7 Federal Infrastructure Funding _To be drafted from D13 SD7 — the synthesis sub-domain. Federal funding channels (direct-recipient, state-pass-through, competitive-grant, cross-jurisdictional) supporting the substantive sub-domains; IIJA reauthorization (Sept 30 2026) as the most consequential near-term federal House lever; Justice40 revocation aftermath; statutory-stability vs administrative-vulnerability taxonomy applied to physical infrastructure programs._
